BALL.chatbotDescription: Ball is a reaction and visual-tracking game. A ball moves continuously around the screen and the player must tap it to catch it before it gets away. Each catch plays a sound and the ball reappears at a new position after a short pause; catching 10 balls ends and wins the game. The ball moves faster at higher levels, leaving less time to react, and tapping near the ball but missing it counts as a wrong tap. The aim is to catch all 10 balls as quickly as possible, so the completion time is the main performance measure (it drives the feedback). A split-screen two-player mode pits two players, each catching their own ball, side by side. Scoring: score1 = balls caught (out of 10), score2 = wrong taps (near-misses around the ball). This game trains visual tracking, hand-eye coordination, reaction speed, and motor precision. Tips: anticipate where the ball is heading rather than chasing where it currently is, tap precisely on the ball since near-misses count against you, and stay relaxed to keep your reactions quick as the ball speeds up at higher levels.

ANIMALS.chatbotDescription: Carnival of the Animals (Animals) is a habitat-matching game played over 10 rounds. Each round shows an image of an animal, and players must tap the environment where that animal lives. At level 1 (easy), there are 3 broad habitats to choose from: sky, earth, and water. At higher levels, there are 8 more specific habitats: farm, sky, domestic, savannah, forest, river, sea ice (floe), and sea. A timer may limit the response time per round; running out of time counts as a wrong answer. Scoring: score1 = correct habitat matches, score2 = wrong matches (including timeouts). This game trains semantic categorization, knowledge of animal habitats, and quick decision-making. Tips: think about where the animal naturally lives day-to-day rather than everywhere it could survive, and for ambiguous animals pick its most iconic or commonly depicted environment.

BLOCK_PUZZLE.chatbotDescription: Block Puzzle challenges players to fit block pieces into a grid to complete rows or patterns. Players drag tetromino-style pieces onto the board. Complete rows or columns disappear. Scoring: score1 = lines cleared, score2 = pieces placed, score3 = highest combo. This game trains spatial reasoning, planning, and visual-motor coordination. Tips: Look ahead at upcoming pieces, keep the grid balanced, prioritize completing full rows.

CALCULUS.chatbotDescription: Calculus is a math training game presenting arithmetic problems (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division). Players see an equation and must select the correct answer from multiple choices. Scoring: score1 = correct answers, score2 = wrong answers. This game trains mental calculation, numerical reasoning, and working memory. Tips: For addition, group numbers that sum to 10; for multiplication, memorize common tables; break complex problems into simpler steps.

CARS.chatbotDescription: Congesting Parking (Cars) is a sliding puzzle game similar to Rush Hour. Players must move cars horizontally or vertically to clear a path for the target car to exit the parking lot. Cars can only move along their orientation axis. Scoring: score1 = moves made, score2 = minimum moves needed to solve, score3 = hints used. This game trains spatial reasoning, planning, and problem-solving. Tips: Identify blocking cars first, plan several moves ahead, and work backwards from the exit.

CASCADE.chatbotDescription: Crazy Waterfall (Cascade) is a spot-the-difference game. Two columns of symbols scroll down together: the left column shows a reference 'model' row, and the right column shows matching buttons where some symbols have been secretly swapped for a different one. Players must tap only the buttons in the right column whose symbol differs from its counterpart on the left, leaving identical symbols untouched. New rows appear automatically on a timer (or via a next-row button if untimed). Each mistake - tapping a symbol that is actually identical, or letting a different symbol pass without tapping it - lights another segment of a fuse on a bomb; too many mistakes makes the bomb explode and ends the game. The game also ends after a fixed number of rows, or after 2 minutes if timed. Scoring: score1 = good answers (differences correctly found plus identical symbols correctly left alone), score2 = bad answers (wrong taps plus differences missed), score3 = differences found, score4 = identical symbols correctly ignored, score5 = wrong taps, score6 = differences missed. This game trains visual discrimination, sustained attention, and impulse control. Tips: compare each symbol in the right column to its counterpart on the left before deciding, work through rows methodically, and avoid tapping out of doubt since both a wrong tap and a missed difference count as mistakes.

CATERPILLAR.chatbotDescription: Operation Caterpillar (Caterpillar) is a math game where players steer a caterpillar's head around the screen - by tilting the device or tapping a target location - to eat food items, each labeled with an arithmetic operation (e.g. +3, -2, x2, /5). It has two modes. In Free (Question) mode, an instruction strip shows a sequence of target values; the caterpillar's tail currently holds a value, and players must eat the one food item whose operation turns that value into the next target in the sequence. A correct choice grows the caterpillar by a segment and reveals the next target; a wrong choice just resets the food options. In Reach 100 mode, the caterpillar's length represents its current value, and players repeatedly pick operations from the food items to bring that value to exactly 100, with the correct food revealed as a hint after enough correct answers. Scoring: score1 = correct choices, score2 = incorrect choices, score3 = average reaction time in milliseconds. This game trains mental arithmetic, planning, and motor control. Tips: work out the result of an operation before steering toward that food, and in Reach 100 mode favor operations that bring the total closer to 100 without overshooting.

CHESSBOARD.chatbotDescription: Crazy Chessboard (Chessboard) is a visual memory game. At the start of each grid, a set of squares briefly flips over to reveal a highlighted pattern, then flips back to hide it. Players must then tap the squares they remember being highlighted. A 'show model' button lets players replay the pattern again, at the cost of using a hint. The game has multiple grids (rounds), with the grid size and number of squares to find increasing with difficulty. Scoring: score1 = correctly identified squares, score2 = incorrectly identified squares, score3 = number of times the model was reviewed (hints used). This game trains visual-spatial memory and concentration. Tips: group the highlighted squares into a shape or pattern to memorize them more easily, and use the 'show model' hint sparingly since reviewing it again is tracked as a hint.

COLORFORM.chatbotDescription: ColorForm is a visual discrimination game where players must quickly identify and tap the shape that matches both a target color AND form simultaneously. A grid of colored shapes is displayed, and players must find the one matching both criteria. Scoring: score1 = correct selections, score2 = wrong selections. This game trains visual discrimination, attention, and cognitive flexibility. Tips: Focus on one attribute first (color or shape), then verify the second; develop systematic scanning patterns.

COLORMIND.chatbotDescription: ColorMind is a color sequence memory game similar to Simon Says. Players observe a sequence of colored canvases lighting up, then must reproduce the sequence by selecting colors in the correct order from left to right. The sequence grows longer with each successful round. Scoring: score1 = sequences completed correctly, score2 = sequences failed. This game trains working memory, sequential recall, and concentration. Tips: Associate colors with positions, verbalize the sequence, chunk colors into groups of 3-4.

COOK.chatbotDescription: Cooking Game challenges players to identify recipe ingredients or quantities. In ingredient mode (levels 1-2), players identify which ingredients belong to a recipe from a grid of options. In recipe mode (level 3), players read cooking instructions and fill in missing ingredients or quantities. No timer - play at your own pace. Scoring: score1 = correct answers, score2 = wrong answers, score3 = hints used. This game trains memory, vocabulary, and attention to detail. Tips: Study the ingredients list carefully, use clues to identify ingredient categories.

FURIOUS.chatbotDescription: Furious is a visual sequence memory game. Players observe a sequence of images displayed in order, then must arrange shuffled cards back into the correct sequential order by dragging them. Intruder cards may be mixed in to increase difficulty. Scoring: score1 = rounds completed correctly, score2 = times 'show answer' was used, score3 = times model was reviewed, score4 = total moves made, score5 = total images across all rounds. This game trains visual memory, sequencing, and attention. Tips: Focus on memorizing the order before cards shuffle, use the review button sparingly, identify and ignore intruder cards.

GEO.chatbotDescription: Geography Quiz has two modes: NameIt (identify the name of a highlighted region on a map from 4 choices) and PlaceIt (tap on the map to find a specific location using clues). Players earn coins for correct answers in PlaceIt and can purchase clues. Regions include US states, European countries, and French departments. Scoring: score1 = correct answers, score2 = wrong answers, score3 = tries remaining (PlaceIt), score4 = times showed result, score5 = clues purchased. This game trains geographic knowledge, spatial recognition, and deductive reasoning. Tips: Use clues strategically, learn neighboring regions, associate locations with distinctive shapes.

HANGMAN.chatbotDescription: Hangman is the classic word-guessing game. Players guess letters to reveal a hidden word before making too many wrong guesses. Each incorrect letter adds a part to the hangman figure. Scoring: score1 = words guessed correctly, score2 = words failed. This game trains vocabulary, spelling, and deductive reasoning. Tips: Start with common vowels (E, A, I, O), then frequent consonants (R, S, T, L, N); consider word length and emerging patterns.

INTRUS.chatbotDescription: Odd One Out (Intrus) presents a grid of items where players must identify the one item that doesn't belong to the same category as the others. The intruder differs semantically from the rest (different category, type, or attribute). Scoring: score1 = correct identifications, score2 = wrong identifications. This game trains categorization, logical reasoning, and semantic knowledge. Tips: Identify the common theme first, consider multiple possible categories, look for subtle differences.

LOST_POEM.chatbotDescription: Lost Poem is an interactive word puzzle where players fill in missing words in a poem by selecting from 4 multiple-choice options per word. Players can view the complete poem as a hint (limited uses by difficulty) and use 50/50 elimination (levels 1-2 only). No timer - play at your own pace. Scoring: score1 = correct word selections, score2 = wrong selections, score3 = times poem was viewed, score4 = 50/50 hints used. This game trains reading comprehension, vocabulary, and memory. Tips: Read context clues around missing words, use poem visualization sparingly.

CYRANO.chatbotDescription: Cyrano is a speech-based recitation game where players read a literary text aloud while the app uses speech recognition to track their progress line by line. If the player hesitates, the app progressively reveals clues by hiding fewer words; using too many clues ends the game. Players can pick a preset text or add their own custom text. Scoring: score1 = completion percent (progress through the text), score2 = number of clues used. This game trains reading fluency, verbal memory, articulation, and confidence in oral expression. Tips: Read at a steady pace, articulate clearly so speech recognition picks up the words, and try to recall lines from memory before relying on clues.

MEMORY.chatbotDescription: Memory Match is the classic card-matching game. Players flip pairs of cards to find matching images, remembering card positions between turns. The goal is to find all pairs with minimum attempts. Scoring: score1 = pairs found, score2 = total flip attempts, score3 = time to complete. This game trains visual memory, concentration, and spatial recall. Tips: Start systematically from one corner, mentally note positions even when cards don't match, use location-based memory strategies.

MUSIC.chatbotDescription: Music Quiz is an audio identification game with 4 modes: Common Sounds, Animal Sounds, Instruments, and Musical Quiz. Players listen to an audio clip (unlimited replays allowed) and select the correct answer from 4 choices. No timer - self-paced gameplay. Scoring: score1 = correct identifications, score2 = wrong identifications. This game trains auditory recognition, memory, and categorization. Tips: Listen carefully before answering, replay audio if unsure, focus on distinctive sound characteristics.

NOAHS_ARK.chatbotDescription: Noah's Ark is a timed matching game where players drag animal cards into Noah's Ark to pair identical animals. Players must match pairs before the timer ends. When 10 seconds remain, the ark starts moving and waves animate. Scoring: score1 = animals matched (pairs × 2), score2 = failed match attempts. This game trains visual matching, quick recognition, and motor coordination. Tips: Look for identical animals, work quickly but accurately, prioritize easy matches first.

PANURGE.chatbotDescription: Panurge's Sheep is a defensive game where players protect bouncing sheep by drawing horizontal or vertical containment lines. The goal is to contain as much area as possible without letting sheep touch the lines (which costs lives). Reaching 80% containment adds a new sheep. Scoring: score1 = final sheep count (difficulty reached), score2 = containment percentage at game end. Lives: 3 starting, bonus life every 4 level-ups. This game trains spatial planning, timing, and strategic thinking. Tips: Draw lines away from sheep, create smaller regions to trap sheep, watch sheep movement patterns before acting.

POEME.chatbotDescription: A Poem A Day (Poem) is a daily reading activity rather than a scored game. Each day the app presents a new poem along with its title, author (with birth/death dates when available), origin, translation, and a short author biography. Players read the poem on screen, can use zoom in/out controls to adjust the text size, and can tap a speaker button to have the poem read aloud via text-to-speech. This activity supports reading comprehension, vocabulary, appreciation of language and rhythm, and general culture. There is no score, time limit, or right/wrong answer - it's a calm, self-paced cultural break. Tips: try reading along while the text-to-speech narrates, and use the resume/biography section to learn more about the author.

PONG.chatbotDescription: Pong is the classic paddle game where players control a paddle to bounce a ball and prevent it from reaching the dead zone. The game ends after 5 misses. Supports single-player and split-screen two-player modes. Difficulty adjusts ball speed and paddle size. Scoring: score1 = successful hits (5 - misses), score2 = misses, score3 = game duration in seconds. This game trains reaction time, hand-eye coordination, and anticipation. Tips: Anticipate ball trajectory, keep paddle centered when possible, watch the ball continuously.

POPBALLOON.chatbotDescription: Pop Balloon is an archery game where players aim a bow and fire arrows to pop falling balloons of a specific target color while avoiding wrong-colored balloons. Balloons fall from the screen edges and players must aim by touch-dragging and release to fire. Scoring: score1 = correct color balloons popped, score2 = total correct color balloons available, score3 = wrong color balloons popped, score4 = total wrong color balloons. This game trains selective attention, motor coordination, and color discrimination. Tips: Focus on the target color shown at top, time your shots carefully, lead moving balloons.

PROVERB.chatbotDescription: Proverb is a word sequencing game where players arrange scrambled proverb words into the correct order by dragging colored word buttons. Players have a time limit per proverb (15-45 seconds depending on difficulty). A pass button allows skipping. Scoring: score1 = proverbs correctly arranged, score2 = proverbs timed out, score3 = proverbs skipped. Difficulty increases word count: level 1 = 4 words, level 2 = 6 words, level 3 = 8 words. This game trains language comprehension, sequencing, and working memory. Tips: Look for sentence starters and endings, identify grammatical patterns, work quickly within time limits.

PUZZLE.chatbotDescription: Jigsaw Puzzle challenges players to assemble image pieces into a complete picture by dragging pieces to their correct positions. Scoring: score1 = pieces placed correctly, score2 = placement attempts, score3 = time to complete. This game trains visual-spatial skills, pattern recognition, and patience.

QUIZZLE.chatbotDescription: Quizzle is a trivia game covering various knowledge categories. Players answer multiple-choice questions with 4 answer options. Scoring: score1 = correct answers, score2 = wrong answers. This game trains general knowledge, recall, and reasoning. Tips: Eliminate obviously wrong answers, use context clues, trust your first instinct on familiar topics.

RELIBULLE.chatbotDescription: Relibulle is a number sequencing game where players click numbered bubbles in ascending order (1, 2, 3, etc.). Bubbles are scattered randomly on screen. An eraser button allows undoing wrong clicks. Difficulty scales by bubble count (level × 10 bubbles). Scoring: score1 = bubbles clicked in correct sequence, score2 = incorrect click attempts. This game trains sequential thinking, visual scanning, and attention. Tips: Scan for the next number before clicking, use the eraser if you make mistakes, work systematically.

SCROLLANDCATCH.chatbotDescription: Flying Balloons (ScrollAndCatch) is a selective attention game. At the start of each round, the app shows one or two target colors (displayed as colored balloon icons in the instructions). Then a batch of colored balloons flies across the screen in animated motion from various directions. Once all balloons have passed, players must select, for each target color, the correct count of balloons of that color from a row of multiple-choice number buttons. A game consists of 3 to 5 rounds. Scoring: score1 = points earned (2 points per target color answered with no mistakes, 1 point if one mistake was made on that color), score2 = wrong button selections, score3 = number of target colors per round, score4 = rounds completed. This game trains selective attention, visual tracking, and counting under distraction. Tips: keep a running mental count only for the target color(s) shown, ignore balloons of other colors, and if tracking two colors at once, count them separately rather than together.

SEQUENCE.chatbotDescription: Sequence Challenge presents number or pattern sequences that players must continue by selecting the next element. Players analyze the pattern rule and choose the correct continuation. Scoring: score1 = correct sequences, score2 = wrong answers. This game trains logical reasoning, pattern recognition, and mathematical thinking. Tips: Look for arithmetic progressions, identify multiplication patterns, check if differences between terms follow a pattern.

SHAPEBOX.chatbotDescription: ShapeBox is a reflex game where shapes move across the screen and players must tap a button when the correct shape (matching a target shape shown) passes through a designated answer zone. Shapes may rotate at higher difficulties. 10 rounds per game. Scoring: score1 = correct shape catches, score2 = total errors (wrong clicks + missed shapes), score3 = shapes missed, score4 = wrong button clicks. This game trains visual attention, shape recognition, and timing. Tips: Watch the target shape carefully, time your button press when the matching shape is in the zone, ignore non-matching shapes.

SIMILI.chatbotDescription: Simili is a visual search game where players must find the two identical images in a grid of similar-looking pictures. Each round presents a grid where exactly two images are the same. Players tap on one of the matching images to score. Scoring: score1 = correct identifications, score2 = wrong selections. This game trains visual discrimination, attention to detail, and scanning skills. Tips: Systematically compare images, look for subtle differences, scan row by row.

SLIDE_MAZE.chatbotDescription: Slide Maze (Slidemaze) is a puzzle game where players guide a character through a board to reach a goal using directional arrow buttons. The character slides in a direction until hitting an obstacle. Avoid death traps (siren symbols) which cost lives. 5 rounds per game. Scoring: score1 = moves in final round, score2 = total moves across all rounds, score3 = minimum moves needed (optimal solution), score4 = resets used, score5 = deaths, score6 = hints used. This game trains spatial planning, sequential thinking, and problem-solving. Tips: Plan your route before moving, use the hint button to see the optimal path, avoid traps by planning multiple moves ahead.

SNAKE.chatbotDescription: Snake is the classic game where players guide a growing snake to eat food while avoiding collisions with walls or its own body. The snake grows longer with each food item eaten. Scoring: score1 = food items eaten, score2 = final snake length. This game trains planning, reaction time, and spatial awareness. Tips: Keep the snake in open areas, plan routes to food, avoid trapping yourself in corners.

SNOWBALL_EFFECT.chatbotDescription: Snowball Effect is a cumulative memory game where items are progressively added to a list and players must remember the growing sequence. After each addition, players must recall all items in order. Scoring: score1 = longest correct sequence, score2 = recall errors. This game trains working memory, sequential recall, and concentration. Tips: Use memory palace technique, create stories linking items, rehearse the list after each addition.

SUDOKU.chatbotDescription: Sudoku is the number-placement puzzle where players fill a 9x9 grid so each row, column, and 3x3 box contains digits 1-9 without repetition. Players tap cells to place numbers. Scoring: score1 = cells filled correctly, score2 = mistakes made, score3 = hints used. This game trains logical reasoning, pattern recognition, and concentration. Tips: Start with rows/columns with most filled numbers, use elimination, look for naked singles and hidden singles.

SYLLABUS.chatbotDescription: Syllabus is a word-building game where players connect syllables from different columns to form words. Syllables are displayed in vertical columns, and players tap syllables from left to right to construct words from the target list. An eraser button allows clearing selections. Scoring: score1 = total syllables used, score2 = total clicks made. Wrong answers = clicks - syllables (excess clicks). Difficulty: level 1 shows words with hint + easy syllables, level 2 hides words + hard syllables, level 3 = mixed categories. This game trains phonological awareness, vocabulary, and language skills. Tips: Sound out words, connect syllables systematically left to right, look for common word patterns.

TANGRAM.chatbotDescription: Tangram is the ancient Chinese puzzle using seven geometric pieces (tans) to form specific target shapes. Players drag and rotate pieces to match a silhouette exactly. Scoring: score1 = puzzles completed, score2 = time taken, score3 = hints used. This game trains spatial reasoning, rotation skills, and geometric thinking. Tips: Identify large shapes first, use trial and error systematically, notice how pieces can combine to form familiar shapes.

TEXT.chatbotDescription: A Text A Day (Text) is a daily reading activity rather than a scored game. Each day the app presents a new short extract of literature (a story or article) along with its title, author (with birth/death dates when available), publication date, category/subcategory, and a short author biography. Players read the text on screen, can use zoom in/out controls to adjust the text size, and can tap a speaker button to have the text read aloud via text-to-speech. This activity supports reading comprehension, vocabulary, and general culture, and the adjustable font size and narration make it accessible for users with visual or reading difficulties. There is no score, time limit, or right/wrong answer - it's a calm, self-paced reading break. Tips: try following along while the text-to-speech narrates, and use the resume/biography section to learn more about the author or work.

TIMELINE.chatbotDescription: Timeline challenges players to place historical events, inventions, or items in chronological order. Players drag cards to position them correctly on a timeline relative to other events. Scoring: score1 = items correctly placed, score2 = items incorrectly placed. This game trains historical knowledge, temporal reasoning, and estimation. Tips: Use reference points you know well, estimate relative dates, group events by era or category.

WALKER.chatbotDescription: Walker is a word-chain game where players create a path of connected words. Each word must start with the last letter(s) of the previous word, forming a chain. Players select words to extend the chain. Scoring: score1 = words in chain, score2 = invalid attempts. This game trains vocabulary, word association, and linguistic flexibility. Tips: Think ahead about available starting letters, build vocabulary of words with useful endings.

WHACKAMOLE.chatbotDescription: Whack-a-Mole is the classic reaction game where players tap moles as they pop up from holes. Some moles require multiple taps (tougher moles), and some moles should not be tapped (friendly moles at medium+ difficulty). Scoring: score1 = moles whacked, score2 = moles missed, score3 = friendly moles wrongly tapped. This game trains reaction time, selective attention, and inhibition control. Tips: Stay alert and centered, identify friendly vs regular moles quickly, don't tap impulsively.

WHO_AM_I.chatbotDescription: Who Am I is a guessing game where players identify a person, character, or thing from progressive clues. Players receive hints and must deduce the answer. Scoring: score1 = correct identifications, score2 = clues needed before correct answer. This game trains deductive reasoning, knowledge recall, and inference. Tips: Start with broad categories, use process of elimination, pay attention to all clues given.

WORDLE.chatbotDescription: Wordle is the word-guessing game where players have attempts to guess a word. After each guess, tiles change color: green = correct letter in correct position, yellow = correct letter in wrong position, gray = letter not in word. Scoring: score1 = words guessed correctly, score2 = total guesses used, score3 = games where word was not found. This game trains vocabulary, deductive reasoning, and strategic thinking. Tips: Start with words containing common letters (E, A, R, T, O, I, S), use color feedback to eliminate possibilities, consider letter positions carefully.
